title: Dynamic workload tokens/sec microbench for core models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Build and maintain a tokens-per-second (tokens/sec) microbenchmark harness that exercises our core model serving paths with realistic, adaptive load profiles and automated p95 regression detection. This harness will be the canonical CI gate for throughput regressions and provide per-model baseline trends for performance tuning and release decisions.

Why this is needed:
- Existing tps probes are static and don’t reflect bursty, multimodal workloads.
- We frequently see regressions only under realistic request interleaving and sequence-length mixes.
- Need earlier detection in CI to prevent runtime regressions reaching Dedicated/Hosted customers.

Scope (in):
- Per-model microbench harness that runs locally and in CI (k8s job).
- Adaptive load profiles: steady-state, spike, ramp, mixed-sequence-length.
- Token-velocity distribution sampling (short/medium/long sequences).
- p95 and p99 latency and tokens/sec tracking with rolling baseline and alerting.
- Integration with existing telemetry (Prometheus metrics + Console dashboards).
- Auto-fail CI on statistically significant regression (>5% p95 or >7% tokens/sec drop vs baseline).

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Full e2e cost accounting or customer-facing SLA guarantees.
- Replacing long-duration sustained throughput stress tests (these remain separate).

Design overview:
- Harness will be a lightweight Go binary (same runtime client lib used in production) that can replay sample prompts and generate token-level request traces.
- Profiles are YAML-configurable and support: target_tokens_per_sec, concurrency, inter-arrival distribution (poisson, fixed, burst), seq_length_mix, kv_cache_priming_pct.
- Baseline storage: time-series baselines stored in a versioned SQLite blob in S3 (small JSON blobs) keyed by model+profile+commit-hash. CI job will fetch baseline and compute deltas.
- Regression detection: use bootstrap confidence intervals over 30 warmup+measurement windows and flag if p95 increases beyond configured threshold or tokens/sec drops below threshold with p<0.05.
- Telemetry hooks emit: tokens_emitted_total, requests_started_total, requests_completed_total, latency_p95_seconds, latency_p99_seconds, effective_tps (tokens/sec) per model and per profile.
- Alerting: CI failure annotated in PR with a link to a synthetic run dashboard and a short diff summary. Failing regression posts to #perf-alerts Slack channel with run id and shortstat.

Implementation plan:
1) Spec YAML for profiles and sequence-length taxonomy (short/med/long/very-long). (Owner: Marco)
2) Harness binary: request generator, KV cache priming option, local replay mode, measurement windows. (Owner: Marco + Kevin)
3) CI k8s job + small runner image; parallelization knobs and node selectors to pin GPU/CPU flavor. (Owner: Infra team)
4) Baseline collection job and dashboard ingestion pipeline. (Owner: Observability)
5) Alerts and PR annotation flow. (Owner: DX + CI)
6) Run a rollout: smoke on canary models -> expand to top 8 production models -> make required CI gate for runtime-1.20.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness runs locally and completes a 10k-token mixed-profile run in under 30 minutes on dev GPU instances.
- CI job executes harness for each relevant model and fails PRs when predefined regression policy is violated.
- Dashboard shows per-model trending for tokens/sec, p95, p99; historical baseline accessible for 90 days.
- Alerts post to #perf-alerts with run metadata and links to traces.
- Documentation: README with profile examples, how to add new models, how to interpret CI failure output.

Risks and mitigations:
- Noise from multi-tenant nodes: mitigate by node selectors and running on isolated infra in CI.
- Baseline drift: define scheduled rebaseline cadence and require a changelog when baselines shift >3%.
- False positives from model nondeterminism: use multiple windows and statistical testing to reduce flakiness.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/TS/Adaptive+TPS+Harness (placeholder)
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX (placeholder)
- Example profile YAML: https://drive.redwood.com/example-profiles/adaptive.yaml (placeholder)

Next steps this week:
- Merge profile spec MR and land a minimal harness prototype that emits metrics (target: 2026-02-22).
- Coordinate with Observability to allocate a dashboard and test metric names.
